newsitem.title: USA: Crews shift gears in battle with Louisiana blowout.
newsitem.headline: Crews shift gears in battle with Louisiana blowout.

text.p: Crews working to extinguish a burning natural gas well in southern Louisiana shifted gears on Thursday after tests indicated the blowout could not be capped by forcing drilling mud down the well, officials said.
"Preliminary indications were not favorable for closing the well using the mud-flow approach," a U.S. Coast Guard spokesman said, adding that crews are now assessing two other options.

The well blew out on Monday in a remote marsh about 40 miles southwest of Baton Rouge, shooting flames about 200 feet into the air and killing four of the 22 workers on a rig barge being used to complete the well.
The fire has been fueled by an estimated 20 million cubic feet a day (mmcfd) of dry natural gas flowing from the well, and crews planned to attempt to shut down the flow as early as Friday.
"We're hoping to make a stab at it tomorrow," said Phil Rykhoek, chief financial officer of well operator Denbury Resources Corp of Dallas.
